items.title: Item 1
items.text: Intel’s Most Advanced Chip Now in Production ----------------------------------------------- Intel (NASDAQ:INTC ) revealed the start of production of its most-advanced chip node at the VLSI Symposium in Honolulu on Tuesday. Named 18A-P, the new chip generation is still at the early “risk production” stage, and aims to help Intel regain its position as a serious competitor in manufacturing chips for third-party customers – following May’s announcement of a deal to make chips for Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL ). * Higher performance for AI workloads: Intel says the 18A-P is also more energy efficient than the previous 18A, while also being compatible so 18A customers won’t face any chip redesigns. * “The sentiment around this stock has absolutely shifted”: Fool contributing analyst Travis Hoium recently noted the market is “starting to think about this company completely differently.” The stock fell 8.45% Tuesday, but recovered some of those losses in early trading today – and it’s outperformed the S&P 500 by 153% since February’s recommendation in Stock Advisor by Team Hidden Gems. items.title: Item 2
items.text: SpaceX Soars Past Amazon’s Market Cap ---------------------------------------- SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX ) jumped for a third straight day Tuesday, closing with a market cap of $2.66 trillion and up 49% from its IPO offer price. That makes it more valuable than Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN ) and just short of Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT ) – which it briefly surpassed – to make it the world’s fourth most valuable company, during the day. Retail investors are competing for just 4.2% of SpaceX shares available for trading following the IPO. * “AI will achieve Stockfish-level coding and generalized computer use”: After SpaceX announced the all-stock acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion, CEO Elon Musk spoke of ambitions for AI to beat humans at producing computer code – using a reference to the world’s current strongest open-source chess engine. * “I am not involved with SpaceX now. Neither short nor, ahem, long”: Michael Burry cast doubt on SpaceX’s valuation, describing the company as “fundamentally a small space company, a niche telecom, a bedeviled social media company, and a CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV ) light.” But he says bearish options are currently too highly priced. Get the Fool take on the SpaceX IPO Divider -----------------------------------------

items.text:
Report: Amazon Under FTC Investigation ----------------------------------------- Amazon – a Stock Advisor Foundational Stock from Team Rule Breakers – could face penalties reaching billions of dollars over claims of misleading advertisers, says Bloomberg. The Federal Trade Commission is reportedly investigating claims Amazon might not have properly disclosed terms and pricing for sponsored listings and sponsored ads. * “Amazon is the third-largest online advertising company”: The report points to the $68.6 billion in advertising revenue Amazon earned last year as evidence of the growing ad impact on future growth for the online giant. * Amazon shrugged: The stock showed little reaction, essentially unchanged in pre-market trading today – just as it was barely affected by last fall’s $2.5 billion settlement over the Prime subscription cancellation process. items.title: Item 4
items.text: Kevin Warsh Takes the Hot Seat --------------------------------- Today’s Federal Reserve interest-rate decision is the first test for new chair Kevin Warsh, as he faces the challenge of “demonstrating that his decisions are grounded in economic fundamentals rather than political considerations” according to Greg Daco of EY-Parthenon. After May’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) saw year-over-year inflation hit 4.2%, analysts expect the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged. * Losing the dot plot?: The Fed’s quarterly chart showing where policymakers expect future rates to go, known as the dot plot, is keenly anticipated. But Wall Street expects Warsh not to take part, possibly because he hasn’t been in office long enough or just because he reportedly doesn’t like it. * How will retail sales impact inflation?: Prior to the meeting, we’ll have the retail sales print for May. Forecasts suggest a modest 0.5% month-over-month rise, and 0.6% excluding auto sales. Track why gas drove inflation to 4.2% Divider -------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 5
items.text: Dividends and Growth Aren’t Mutually Exclusive ------------------------------------------------- Anthony Schiavone ANTHONY SCHIAVONE I think there’s a common misconception among executives and investors that a company with an above-average dividend yield – or even just a dividend at all – can’t be a growth company. I couldn’t disagree more. Dividends and growth are not mutually exclusive. Consider the five largest dividend payers in the world by market cap. Every one of them has outperformed the S&P 500 since initiating its dividend – and not by a little. I’m not saying that dividend stocks are inherently better than non-dividend stocks, or vice versa. I’m saying that growth and dividends are not mutually exclusive. So if you’re hunting for growth, don’t reflexively dismiss a company simply because it pays a dividend. Crack the dividend vs growth myth Divider -----------------------------------------------

items.text: Today’s Take: Volatile Stock or Risky Stock? ----------------------------------------------- Sanmeet Deo A high-risk company frequently exhibits high volatility, but the inverse is not always true. Crucially, when volatility is high but fundamental risk is low, investors encounter compelling opportunities. — SANMEET DEO • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to add how you think about the difference between a stock that's volatile and a stock that's actually risky, or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today!
